2027-12-24 and 2027-12-27: 24, 25 and 26 December are public holidays; 25 December is a Saturday and 26 December a Sunday, so the weekend rule (section 53-5-30) gives Friday 24 December and Monday 27 December

laws.rule: The South Carolina Hands-Free and Distracted Driving Act (Code 56-5-3890, rewritten by 2025 Act No. 40, in force 1 September 2025) bans drivers on public roads from holding or supporting a phone or other mobile device with any part of the body; reading, writing or sending texts, emails, app or web content; and watching video, games or video calls. Voice calls through an earpiece or watch, voice-to-text without holding the device, and hands-free navigation and audio are allowed, as is use while lawfully parked or stopped and to report an emergency. Only warnings were given for the first 180 days.
laws.penalty_signal: US$100 first offence; US$200 and 2 licence points for a later offence within 3 years (about A$142 and A$284 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040). Fines can't be suspended.

laws.rule: South Carolina law (Code of Laws 23-35-130) makes it unlawful to manufacture, store, transport or possess fireworks with more than two grains of pyrotechnic composition made to give a loud, piercing effect, such as ground salutes, cherry bombs, M-80s, T-N-T salutes and bulldog salutes. Under 23-35-175, a condominium association can file for a fireworks-prohibited zone, and knowingly discharging fireworks into one is a misdemeanour. Penalties in the chapter: a fine of up to US$200 or up to 30 days for a first offence (about A$284 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026).

items.text: Marijuana is a Schedule I controlled substance in South Carolina. Possessing 1 ounce (28 g) or less is a misdemeanour: for a first offence, up to 30 days in jail or a fine of US$100 to US$200 (about A$142 to A$284 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040); for a second or later offence, up to 1 year or a fine of US$200 to US$1,000 (Code 44-53-370(d)(5)).

Retail liquor stores may not sell spirits between 7 pm and 9 am (Code 61-6-1500), and must close on Christmas Day. They may not sell on Sundays, except in counties and cities that have approved Sunday sales by referendum and where the store holds a Sunday permit from the Department of Revenue (Code 61-6-4160). Bills to widen Sunday sales were before the 2025 to 2026 Legislature.
